review_cost.rationale: I'd approve after one small round: add an ErrorBoundary, extract the duplicated param coercion, and either split queries.ts or accept it as the data layer with a comment on its caching strategy; nothing else rises above nits.

findings.issue: No ErrorBoundary anywhere; @solidjs/router docs state a throwing query is caught by the nearest ErrorBoundary, so API failures (fetchJson throws on non-OK, app/src/lib/queries.ts:163-171) become unhandled rejections with a stuck Suspense fallback.
findings.suggestion: Wrap {props.children} in an <ErrorBoundary> with a fallback (e.g. 'Something went wrong' plus a link home) inside the Router root.

findings.issue: Single 700-line data module holds HTTP caching, three module-level caches, DTO types and all six page queries; the god data module everything else imports.
findings.suggestion: Split per resource (species.ts, moves.ts, types.ts …) with a shared api.ts for fetchJson/apiBase; keeps per-page queries reviewable as pages evolve.

findings.issue: Debounced search is hand-rolled: signal + manual lastUrlSearch tracking + createEffect DOM sync, a home-grown equivalent of reactive search params; pagination hrefs (index.tsx:181) read the signal, so they can diverge from the URL q while a debounce is pending.
findings.suggestion: Derive the displayed list and hrefs from the URL params (or commit the debounced value before building hrefs), and isolate the input-sync logic behind a small useDebouncedSearchParam helper with a comment on why attr:value is used.

findings.issue: Manual scroll-to-#moves effect refires whenever data() changes (e.g. switching game re-scrolls to #moves) and races image layout shifts.
findings.suggestion: Track the last-scrolled hash so the effect runs once per hash entry, or rely on the browser anchor after the streaming Suspense resolves.

findings.issue: paramValue coercion duplicated (gameParam variant in app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:155-158); two near-identical helpers for useSearchParams values.
findings.suggestion: Move a single paramValue helper to src/lib/ (e.g. router.ts) and use it in both routes.

findings.issue: Unexplained domain constants scattered in code: methodPriority, EXCLUDED_TYPES, the id > 10000 alternate-form cutoff; the codebase has zero comments (commentLines: 0).
findings.suggestion: One-line comments on why (spec rules: alternate forms excluded, fixed method ordering, excluded pseudo-types) so future maintainers don't re-derive them from SPEC.md.

findings.issue: Build tooling (vite, nitro) declared as runtime dependencies, with nitro pinned to an exact beta build '3.0.260610-beta'.
findings.suggestion: Move vite and nitro to devDependencies (they're build-time plugins) and use a caret range for nitro, or document why the exact pin is required.

findings.issue: Fact-list dl markup duplicated between move and pokemon summary sections (class names differ: fact-list vs measures), a small near-identical-helper risk as pages grow.
findings.suggestion: Optional: extract a small FactList component for labelled key/value description lists shared across routes.

summary: A clean, current-stable SolidStart v2 app that uses the framework's documented primitives correctly (query+createAsync, FileRoutes, Nitro-via-Vite config, HttpStatusCode 404s) and passes review with only one substantive change request: an ErrorBoundary, whose absence turns API errors into unhandled rejections. The single 700-line queries.ts data module is the main structural nit, and the hand-rolled search-input debounce and #moves scroll are small workarounds worth tidying. I'd merge after a light round of fixes.
